etymologies.etymologyHTML: From offer +‎ -ing.

definitions.definition: The act by which something is offered.
That which has been offered; a sacrifice.
An oblation or presentation made as a religious act.

quote.citation: 1995, Glen Dudbridge, Religious Experience and Lay Society in T'ang China: a reading of Tai Fu's Kuang-i chi‎[1], Cambridge University Press, →ISBN, →LCCN, →OCLC, pages 69–70:
quote.text: In many ways an ancient well-established situation is in Place: a dead military hero has reappeared as a ghost bringing trouble and even death to the officials who come to administer the Hsiang-chou prefecture at An-yang; they build a temple in his honour and make him regular offerings of bloody food; he then protects and supports the administrators who are responsible.

definitions.definition: A contribution given at a religious service.
Something put forth, bid, proffered or tendered, such as for sale

quote.text: In recent seasons fetishwear has found its way onto the catwalk, with vinyl, PVC and lycra featuring among the most unlikely designer offerings.

definitions.definition: present participle and gerund of offer

quote.citation: 2013 June 21, Oliver Burkeman, “The tao of tech”, in The Guardian Weekly, volume 189, number 2, page 27:
quote.text: The dirty secret of the internet is that all this distraction and interruption is immensely profitable. Web companies like to boast about […], or offering services that let you "stay up to date with what your friends are doing", […] and so on. But the real way to build a successful online business is to be better than your rivals at undermining people's control of their own attention.
